---
title: "1. Counts and quality control"
---

## The starting object: a gene-by-cell matrix

A droplet-based scRNA-seq experiment ultimately gives us a sparse matrix. Rows are genes, columns are cell barcodes, and entries are usually UMI counts.

| Gene | Cell A | Cell B | Cell C |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CD3D | 8 | 11 | 0 |
| NKG7 | 16 | 2 | 0 |
| MS4A1 | 0 | 0 | 14 |
| LST1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

The analysis pipeline does not begin with clusters or UMAP. It begins with the question: **which columns are credible representations of intact single cells?**

## What a zero means

A zero is not automatically biological absence. It can mean low expression, sampling failure, limited library depth, or true absence. This is why interpreting one gene in one cell is risky; stable programs across many genes/cells are more reliable.

## Three common QC summaries

### `nFeature_RNA`
Number of genes detected in a cell. Extremely low values can indicate empty/poor droplets; unusually high values can indicate multiplets.

### `nCount_RNA`
Total UMI count. High `nCount_RNA` often accompanies high `nFeature_RNA`, but the relationship should be inspected rather than thresholded blindly.

### mitochondrial percentage
A high mitochondrial fraction can accompany damaged/stressed cells because cytoplasmic RNA is lost disproportionately.

```r
obj[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^MT-")
VlnPlot(obj, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
```

Our synthetic metadata already contains a pedagogical `percent.mt` variable, so you can explore its distribution even though the synthetic count matrix does not contain mitochondrial genes.

## Why universal cutoffs are a mistake

A lymphocyte may naturally contain fewer detected genes than a malignant epithelial cell. A fixed rule such as `nFeature_RNA < 5000` can therefore remove legitimate cells in one tissue and fail to remove doublets in another.

A better workflow is:

1. examine each sample separately;
2. visualize joint relationships (`nCount` vs `nFeature`, mitochondrial fraction vs counts);
3. consider tissue biology;
4. use doublet detection when appropriate;
5. document the exact thresholds and sensitivity analyses.

```r
FeatureScatter(obj, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA")
```

::: {.callout-important}
QC is not cosmetic cleanup. Filtering changes the population on which every subsequent mean, variance, PC loading, neighborhood, and cluster will be calculated.
:::
